person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether short-term synaptic plasticity can be seen at work in an intact brain during behaviour
span.quote: However, in contrast to the large body of experiments that focus on neuronal firing patterns, relatively little empirical research 14 – 16 bears on short-term synaptic plasticity in the intact brain during behavior, and therefore its significance with respect to behavioral and cognitive processes remains largely theoretical.

span.label: monosynaptic efficacy varies with position and trajectory in a working memory task, beyond what co-varying firing rates can explain
span.quote: On finer timescales, putative monosynaptic interactions reflected short-term plasticity in their dynamic and predictable modulation across various aspects of the task, beyond a statistical accounting for the effect of the neurons’ co-varying firing rates.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Monosynaptic interactions between pairs of neurons varied dynamically during the task and might be explained by the demonstrated short-term facilitation and suppression of synaptic strengths and the supralinear postsynaptic effect of the coincident firing of two or more presynaptic neurons.

span.label: behaviour-dependent short-term synaptic plasticity in prefrontal cortex
span.quote: Here we looked for the signature of short-term plasticity in the fine-timescale spiking relationships of a simultaneously recorded population of physiologically identified pyramidal cells and interneurons, in the medial prefrontal cortex of the rat, in a working memory task.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: During the recording sessions, neurophysiological signals were acquired continuously at 20 kHz on a 128-channel DataMax system (16-bit resolution; RC Electronics).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Short-term synaptic facilitation and depression modulate spike transmission, so sequentially discharging neurons form internally generated assemblies whose lifetimes are set by changing synaptic efficacies
span.note: status: the paper's own words: We hypothesize that
span.quote: We hypothesize that sequentially discharging neurons reflect internally generated cell assemblies, whose dynamics are in turn supported by the modulation of synaptic efficacies.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Supersynchronous presynaptic input triggers dendritic spikes in the target interneuron, producing supralinear summation of coincident inputs
span.quote: One mechanism underlying the supralinear summation effect might be the initiation of dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Neuronal reverberation: a receding assembly hands its representational content to a successor assembly, generating the ordered firing sequence
span.quote: A potential interpretation of the orderly sequence of neuronal firing is that firing patterns reflect a neuronal representation of goals and movement trajectories through ‘neuronal reverberation’

span.label: one presynaptic neuron's increased activity can reduce its control of an interneuron while another's increases it, on the same postsynaptic cell
span.quote: We also observed the combination of these effects on single cells, showing that, for a given interneuron, increased activity from one presynaptic neuron can reduce that neuron’s control of the interneuron (depression), whereas increased activity from another presynaptic neuron can increase that neuron’s control of the interneuron.

span.label: that opposite pattern on one cell argues for synaptic mechanisms rather than passive membrane properties
span.quote: These latter findings also argue in favor of synaptic mechanisms rather than passive membrane properties

span.label: coincident discharge of two or more presynaptic neurons within 5 ms raises the target's firing probability supralinearly
span.quote: A second mechanism that affected spike transmission between cell pairs depended on the precise timing of the various inputs. Coincident discharge of two or more pre-synaptic neurons within a 5-ms time window increased, in a supra-linear fashion, the probability of a target interneuron’s discharge.

span.label: dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs are offered as a mechanism for that supralinearity
span.quote: One mechanism underlying the supralinear summation effect might be the initiation of dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs, as shown in hippocampal neurons 30 . Such dendritic boosting may be particularly prominent in certain interneuron types because of the high densities of voltage-gated sodium and potassium ion channels in distal dendrites

span.label: sequences may reflect a receding assembly handing its content to the next, with lifetimes set by internal mechanisms including short-term plasticity
span.quote: A potential interpretation of the orderly sequence of neuronal firing is that firing patterns reflect a neuronal representation of goals and movement trajectories through ‘neuronal reverberation’ 1 , wherein a receding assembly gives rise to another cell assembly, which lasts for a similar duration before passing its representational ‘content’ to further assemblies. Under this scenario, the ‘lifetimes’ of neuronal activity are controlled by internal mechanisms, among which might belong the demonstrated short-term synaptic plasticity. We hypothesize that sequentially discharging neurons reflect internally generated cell assemblies, whose dynamics are in turn supported by the modulation of synaptic efficacies.

span.label: Only a small, possibly unrepresentative fraction of neurons and connections could be observed.
span.note: what this limits: any population-level or connectivity claim: ONLY A SMALL PERCENTAGE OF NEURONS AND THEIR CONNECTIONS COULD BE MONITORED IN OUR STUDY
span.quote: Despite the high-density recordings provided by silicon probes, only a small percentage of neurons and their connections could be monitored in our study

span.label: Synaptic connections are inferred indirectly from extracellular cross-correlograms, not measured.
span.note: what this limits: every reported synaptic connection: MONOSYNAPTIC INTERACTIONS CAN ONLY BE INDIRECTLY INFERRED FROM AN EXTRACELLULAR SIGNAL - inferred, not measured
span.quote: Monosynaptic interactions can only be indirectly inferred from an extracellular signal.

span.label: The cross-correlation method is insensitive to weak pyramidal-to-pyramidal interactions.
span.note: what this limits: the absence of weak pyramidal-to-pyramidal effects specifically: THE CROSS-CORRELATION METHOD MAY NOT RELIABLY DETECT AND ANALYZE WEAK EXCITATORY INTERACTIONS AMONG PRINCIPAL CELLS - a null here is not evidence of absence
span.quote: Thus, although the cross-correlation method may not reliably detect and analyze weak excitatory interactions among principal cells

span.label: The jitter window size was a judgement call, which qualifies literal reading of the significance values.
span.note: what this limits: the significance values themselves: CHOOSING THE SIZE OF THE JITTER WINDOW WAS A MATTER OF JUDGMENT, AND THIS SHOULD BE KEPT IN MIND IN THE LITERAL INTERPRETATION OF SIGNIFICANCE
span.quote: Nevertheless, choosing the size of the jitter window was a matter of judgment, and this should be kept in mind in the literal interpretation of significance.

span.label: The position-dependence analysis is example-based, without corrections for multiple comparisons across cells.
span.note: what this limits: the position-dependence analysis: OUR APPROACH HERE IS EXAMPLE-BASED, AND WE DID NOT EXPLICITLY COMPUTE MULTIPLE-COMPARISONS CONTROLS ACROSS CELLS
span.quote: Our approach here is example-based, and we did not explicitly compute multiple-comparisons controls across cells.

span.label: The population firing-rate estimates need confirmation by more direct methods.
span.note: what this limits: the population firing-rate estimates only: THE PRESENT ESTIMATES SHOULD BE CONFIRMED BY FUTURE STUDIES USING MORE DIRECT METHODS
span.quote: The present estimates should be confirmed by future studies using more direct methods.

span.label: only a small percentage of neurons could be monitored, most are silent or sparsely active, and the population estimates are stated to need more direct methods
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the added reason that most neurons are silent or sparsely active and so never enter the sample
span.quote: Despite the high-density recordings provided by silicon probes, only a small percentage of neurons and their connections could be monitored in our study (see Supplementary Note ). Because of current limitations in the extracellular method, only neurons with < 60 μm lateral distance from recording sites in the hippocampus generate spikes with sufficiently large amplitudes to be reliably separated into single-neuron clusters 32 . Assuming a similar spike amplitude attenuation in mPFC, the number of recordable neurons from a cylinder of 60-μm radius around each shank corresponds to approximately 60–100 neurons from layer 2/3 and 60 from layer 5 (ref. 22 ), corresponding to a total of 480 to 800 neurons in the volume surveyed by the eight recording shanks. Of these, only approximately 10–25% were active enough in aspects of our task to be clustered. Taking into consideration the ‘silent’ majority, the global firing rate of the population can be estimated as 0.2–0.6 Hz, although individual neurons could robustly increase their spike rates according to task demands. A similar conclusion can be reached by assessing the population synchrony. Of the active minority, on average, approximately 10% of layer 2/3 and 20% of layer 5 neurons fired at least one spike in any 100-ms time window, suggesting that only 1 to 5% of all (active and ‘silent’) neurons fired in synchrony. The present estimates should be confirmed by future studies using more direct methods.

span.label: the cross-correlation method may not reliably detect weak excitatory interactions between principal cells, though it works for principal-to-interneuron connections
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - weak excitatory interactions among principal cells
span.quote: Thus, although the cross-correlation method may not reliably detect and analyze weak excitatory interactions among principal cells 5 (see caveats discussed in Supplementary Note ), it can effectively identify monosynaptic connections between principal cells and interneurons

span.label: the observed principal-to-interneuron ratio is lower than anatomy predicts, attributed to the recording method or to silent principal cells
span.note: what this limits: any use of the cell-type composition as an anatomical estimate: the observed ratio IS LOWER THAN would be expected from anatomy, and the authors attribute the difference to the recording method
span.quote: The ratio of putative principal cells to inhibitory interneurons in the entire population, identified by physiological criteria, was 2.82 ± 0.51 (s.d.). This ratio is lower than would be predicted from the anatomically identified fraction of interneurons in the neocortex (pyramidal/interneuron ≈ 4) 27 but can be explained by the recording method and/or the silent or sparse activity of most principal cells

span.label: the layer difference in trajectory selectivity is reported with the caveat that firing rate differences could influence it
span.note: what this limits: the layer difference in trajectory selectivity: the authors report it with the caveat that firing-rate differences between layers could contribute to the effect
span.quote: The fraction of trajectory-selective neurons in the side arms (positions 0.5–1) was almost twice as large in deep (layer 5, 40%) than in superficial (layer 2/3, 22%) neurons (although firing rate differences could influence this finding

span.label: conditional inference by surrogate construction, with the null chosen to preserve every timescale but the one under test
span.quote: Because the jittered data sets preserve firing rates on timescales much broader than that of the jitter interval, the overall effect of the analysis is to identify as monosynaptic those pairs that showed excess co-firing at short latencies that cannot be accounted for by firing rates varying only at timescales of tens of milliseconds

span.label: thinning - deleting observations at random until a nuisance variable is flat - imported as a power control
span.quote: To more rigorously demonstrate position-dependent monosynaptic effects (the statistical issue is one of power; see Methods), we used a heuristic randomization argument based on thinning. For a given cell pair, we randomly and iteratively removed spikes occurring in maze segment(s) of interest until the remaining (‘thinned’) spikes were uniformly distributed in different maze segments for both cells (that is, so that the thinned spike trains had rates that were ‘flat’, with less than 10% rate variation) and then used the jittering technique to assess position dependence of monosynaptic activity.

span.label: spike trains were jittered at a chosen timescale and the co-firing recomputed, so that only excess co-firing at the FINE timescale survives
span.note: eliminates: that a co-firing pair is explained by shared slow input rather than by a monosynaptic connection - co-firing at broad timescales is common without any direct connection
span.quote: Thus, it is necessary to rule out co-firing exclusively at broad timescales because co-firing in the absence of a monosynaptic interaction becomes far more plausible when it is at broader timescales (as due to common input from many shared presynaptic neurons, for example) 24 , 25 .

span.label: the timing of the interaction was compared against what a passive membrane could produce
span.note: eliminates: that the temporal structure is a passive electrical artefact - the membrane time constant or a changing input conductance in the postsynaptic cell
span.quote: This illustration indicates that the temporal effects of neuronal interactions cannot be explained by passive mechanisms, such as the membrane time constant or rapidly changing input conductance in the postsynaptic neuron, but most likely reflect synaptic mechanisms 5 , 10 .

span.label: supralinear
span.quote: One mechanism underlying the supralinear summation effect might be the initiation of dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs, as shown in hippocampal neurons 30 . Such dendritic boosting may be particularly prominent in certain interneuron types because of the high densities of voltage-gated sodium and potassium ion channels in distal dendrites

span.label: dendritic spikes
span.quote: One mechanism underlying the supralinear summation effect might be the initiation of dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs, as shown in hippocampal neurons 30 . Such dendritic boosting may be particularly prominent in certain interneuron types because of the high densities of voltage-gated sodium and potassium ion channels in distal dendrites

span.label: variation in firing rates → detectability
span.note: RULED OUT BY THE AUTHORS AS AN EXPLANATION: because spikes are uniformly distributed across maze positions, the observed differences in monosynaptic activity are LESS LIKELY TO BE DUE TO firing-rate variation acting on detectability. A control argument, not a relation that holds - and no edge type can say a relation FAILS.
span.quote: The argument is then that, all other things being equal, because the spikes are uniformly distributed in maze positions, differences in monosynaptic activity as a function of position are less likely to be due to the effect of variation in firing rates on detectability (that is, power

span.label: MONOSYNAPTIC here is an inference to the simpler explanation, not an observation - the named rival is shared input producing co-firing without any synapse, and the criterion that separates them is TIMESCALE
span.quote: That is, monosynaptic interaction is chosen as simpler than the alternative explanation that the temporal relationship in spiking is due to temporal relationships between the two neurons’ inputs in the absence of a monosynaptic interaction 18 . Thus, it is necessary to rule out co-firing exclusively at broad timescales because co-firing in the absence of a monosynaptic interaction becomes far more plausible when it is at broader timescales

span.label: the surrogate is built so that its null contains everything EXCEPT the timescale of interest: jittering by ±5 ms preserves firing rates at broader timescales, so what survives cannot be explained by rate variation at tens of milliseconds
span.quote: Because the jittered data sets preserve firing rates on timescales much broader than that of the jitter interval, the overall effect of the analysis is to identify as monosynaptic those pairs that showed excess co-firing at short latencies that cannot be accounted for by firing rates varying only at timescales of tens of milliseconds

span.label: functional synaptic efficacy is defined operationally as the magnitude of excess coincident spikes at short latency - it is a spike-count statistic, not a measured synaptic quantity
span.quote: The functional synaptic efficacy (defined operationally as the magnitude of excess coincidental spikes at short latencies between the pre-and postsynaptic neuron; Supplementary Fig. 9 ) between functionally connected pairs was not constant throughout a trial or during the intertrial interval but varied as a function of position ( Fig. 4 ) and as a function of left versus right trajectory.

span.label: the independence assumption used by the standard shift-predictor approach is rejected here BY NAME, because broad-timescale effects alone can push short-latency co-occurrence above chance
span.quote: Seeking more formal criteria for large scale analysis, a standard approach is to assume that spike trains are independent of one another (that is, precisely, that the response of one neuron is conditionally exchangeable across trials, or shifts, given the other neuron) and then to infer a monosynaptic interaction when the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets is greater than would be expected under independence 15 – 18 , as in the shift predictor. However, such an identification may be confounded by effects occurring more slowly than the timescale of synaptic action: broad-timescale effects alone can cause the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets to exceed that expected under independence

span.label: the confound being controlled is DETECTABILITY rather than the effect: more spikes make a connection easier to detect, so a position-dependent rate would produce position-dependent detection with no change in efficacy
span.quote: Although a minimum co-firing between partner neurons is a prerequisite for the detection of functional connectivity, the effect of firing rates on detection alone can be dissociated from putative monosynaptic mechanisms, provided that large numbers of spikes are available.

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Seeking potential mechanisms for such effects, we found evidence for both firing pattern–dependent facilitation and depression, as well as for a supralinear effect of presynaptic coincidence on the firing of postsynaptic targets.

span.label: method: eight-shank silicon probe recording with jitter-surrogate cross-correlogram analysis and a spike-thinning control for detection power
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: To disambiguate multiple-timescale effects, we used jitter techniques 26 to infer monosynaptic connections. Each spike in each neuron in the original data set was randomly and independently perturbed (or ‘jittered’) on a uniform interval of [−5,+5] ms to form a surrogate data set. The process was repeated independently 1,000 times to form many such surrogate data sets.

span.label: phenomenon: excess short-latency coincident spiking between a pyramidal cell and an interneuron, changing systematically across the maze
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: behaviour-dependent short-term synaptic plasticity in prefrontal cortex — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: The functional synaptic efficacy (defined operationally as the magnitude of excess coincidental spikes at short latencies between the pre-and postsynaptic neuron; Supplementary Fig. 9 ) between functionally connected pairs was not constant throughout a trial or during the intertrial interval but varied as a function of position ( Fig. 4 ) and as a function of left versus right trajectory.

span.label: replicates → previous studies reporting that short-timescale cross-correlations between neuron pairs vary with behaviour (refs 14-16, 33)
span.quote: Similarly to previous studies, we observed that short-term (~5 ms) cross-correlations between pairs of neurons varied as a function of behavior

span.label: contradicts → those earlier studies' assumption that behaviourally varying short-latency cross-correlation peaks reflect pyramidal-pyramidal interactions
span.quote: In contrast, taking into account physiological criteria to separate excitatory and inhibitory neurons, our analysis indicated that most such short-latency peaks in cross-correlograms were likely to correspond to monosynaptic excitation of GABAergic interneurons by their presynaptic pyramidal cells

span.label: extends → prior in vitro observations that excitatory inputs from different sources onto the same interneuron can be depressing or potentiating (refs 2, 5)
span.quote: These observations support previous in vitro observations that excitatory inputs from different sources to the same interneuron can possess either depressing or potentiating properties

span.label: reinterprets → earlier reports of behaviour-dependent short-term cross-correlations, assumed to reflect pyramidal-to-pyramidal interactions
span.quote: In these earlier studies, such short-term effects, often described as ‘functional’ connectivity 34 , were assumed to reflect pyramidal-pyramidal interactions and to correspond to hypothetical physiological mechanisms underlying associative mechanisms, learning, memory or reward expectancy. In contrast, taking into account physiological criteria to separate excitatory and inhibitory neurons, our analysis indicated that most such short-latency peaks in cross-correlograms were likely to correspond to monosynaptic excitation of GABAergic interneurons by their presynaptic pyramidal cells

span.label: extends → in vitro evidence that pyramidal-to-interneuron synapses are plastic over tens to hundreds of milliseconds
span.quote: However, in contrast to the large body of experiments that focus on neuronal firing patterns, relatively little empirical research 14 – 16 bears on short-term synaptic plasticity in the intact brain during behavior, and therefore its significance with respect to behavioral and cognitive processes remains largely theoretical.

span.label: builds-on → jitter and surrogate methods for separating fine-timescale from broad-timescale synchrony
span.quote: To disambiguate multiple-timescale effects, we used jitter techniques 26 to infer monosynaptic connections. Each spike in each neuron in the original data set was randomly and independently perturbed (or ‘jittered’) on a uniform interval of [−5,+5] ms to form a surrogate data set. The process was repeated independently 1,000 times to form many such surrogate data sets.

span.label: critiques → the independence assumption underlying shift-predictor identification of monosynaptic connections
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS THE INDEPENDENCE ASSUMPTION, STATED PRECISELY IN THE SPAN. 'Seeking more formal criteria for large scale analysis, a standard approach is TO ASSUME THAT SPIKE TRAINS ARE INDEPENDENT OF ONE ANOTHER (that is, precisely, that THE RESPONSE OF ONE NEURON IS CONDITIONALLY EXCHANGEABLE ACROSS TRIALS, or shifts...).' The shift predictor is not wrong as arithmetic; it rests on an assumption the paper names in its formal form. Q-444.
span.quote: Seeking more formal criteria for large scale analysis, a standard approach is to assume that spike trains are independent of one another (that is, precisely, that the response of one neuron is conditionally exchangeable across trials, or shifts, given the other neuron) and then to infer a monosynaptic interaction when the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets is greater than would be expected under independence 15 – 18 , as in the shift predictor. However, such an identification may be confounded by effects occurring more slowly than the timescale of synaptic action: broad-timescale effects alone can cause the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets to exceed that expected under independence

span.label: monosynaptic —operationalised-as→ cross-correlogram
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — it can ONLY be inferred indirectly from an extracellular signal - the paper opens the section by saying so
span.quote: Monosynaptic interactions can only be indirectly inferred from an extracellular signal. This is typically done by examining counts of co-occurrences of spiking in the putative pre- and postsynaptic neurons at various differential time lags, as exemplified by the cross-correlogram

span.label: monosynaptic —distinct-from→ firing rates
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS THE TIMESCALE AT WHICH CO-FIRING COUNTS AS A CONNECTION. 'BECAUSE THE JITTERED DATA SETS PRESERVE FIRING RATES ON TIMESCALES MUCH BROADER THAN THAT OF THE JITTER INTERVAL, the overall effect of the analysis is to IDENTIFY AS MONOSYNAPTIC THOSE PAIRS THAT SHOWED EXCESS CO-FIRING AT SHORT LATENCIES THAT CANNOT BE ACCOUNTED FOR BY FIRING R[ATES].' The category is DEFINED BY WHAT A CONTROL CANNOT EXPLAIN, so `monosynaptic` here means `unexplained by rate at this jitter interval` - and the interval is an analyst choice. Q-475. · strength of the relation: 1 — THE NULL CONTAINS EVERYTHING BUT THE TIMESCALE OF INTEREST: jittering preserves rates at broader timescales, so surviving coincidences cannot be rate effects at tens of milliseconds
span.quote: Because the jittered data sets preserve firing rates on timescales much broader than that of the jitter interval, the overall effect of the analysis is to identify as monosynaptic those pairs that showed excess co-firing at short latencies that cannot be accounted for by firing rates varying only at timescales of tens of milliseconds

span.label: jitter —operationalised-as→ monosynaptic
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — 1,000 surrogates, each spike moved independently within ±5 ms
span.quote: To disambiguate multiple-timescale effects, we used jitter techniques 26 to infer monosynaptic connections. Each spike in each neuron in the original data set was randomly and independently perturbed (or ‘jittered’) on a uniform interval of [−5,+5] ms to form a surrogate data set. The process was repeated independently 1,000 times to form many such surrogate data sets.

span.label: monosynaptic —distinct-from→ jitter
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — THE ASSUMPTION REJECTED BY NAME elsewhere: under independence, broad-timescale effects alone can push short-latency co-occurrence above chance, so a jitter surrogate replaces it
span.quote: To disambiguate multiple-timescale effects, we used jitter techniques 26 to infer monosynaptic connections. Each spike in each neuron in the original data set was randomly and independently perturbed (or ‘jittered’) on a uniform interval of [−5,+5] ms to form a surrogate data set. The process was repeated independently 1,000 times to form many such surrogate data sets.

span.label: thinning —distinct-from→ power
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — DISCARD DATA TO MAKE THE CONFOUND CONSTANT: spikes are deleted at random until rates are flat across positions, so position-dependent detectability cannot produce the result
span.quote: To more rigorously demonstrate position-dependent monosynaptic effects (the statistical issue is one of power; see Methods), we used a heuristic randomization argument based on thinning. For a given cell pair, we randomly and iteratively removed spikes occurring in maze segment(s) of interest until the remaining (‘thinned’) spikes were uniformly distributed in different maze segments for both cells (that is, so that the thinned spike trains had rates that were ‘flat’, with less than 10% rate variation) and then used the jittering technique to assess position dependence of monosynaptic activity.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN ARGUES AGAINST A CAUSAL ROLE AND THE EDGE ASSERTS ONE) · power —causes→ firing rates
span.note: RETRACTED: THE SPAN ARGUES AGAINST A CAUSAL ROLE AND THE EDGE ASSERTS ONE. The edge is `power --causes--> firing rates`. The span is a control argument: 'BECAUSE the spikes are uniformly distributed in maze positions, differences in monosynaptic activity as a function of position are LESS LIKELY TO BE DUE TO the effect of variation in firing rates on detectability (that is, power'. The authors are RULING OUT firing-rate variation as an explanation of their result - the negation of the relation the edge records. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): a negative, housed below. FOURTH INSTANCE TONIGHT of the polarity gap - after Colgin2016 (does not hold), Osman2018 (inverse, later reclassified as a correlation) and Pereira2020 (undetermined) - and the only reason it is recorded at all is that `unhoused_relations` exists. — strength of the relation: 1 — the confound is DETECTABILITY, not the effect - more spikes make a connection easier to see
span.quote: The argument is then that, all other things being equal, because the spikes are uniformly distributed in maze positions, differences in monosynaptic activity as a function of position are less likely to be due to the effect of variation in firing rates on detectability (that is, power

span.label: pyramidal —causes→ interneuron
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — THE REATTRIBUTION: earlier work read the same short-latency peaks as pyramidal-to-pyramidal; with physiological classification they are mostly pyramidal-to-interneuron
span.quote: In these earlier studies, such short-term effects, often described as ‘functional’ connectivity 34 , were assumed to reflect pyramidal-pyramidal interactions and to correspond to hypothetical physiological mechanisms underlying associative mechanisms, learning, memory or reward expectancy. In contrast, taking into account physiological criteria to separate excitatory and inhibitory neurons, our analysis indicated that most such short-latency peaks in cross-correlograms were likely to correspond to monosynaptic excitation of GABAergic interneurons by their presynaptic pyramidal cells

span.label: short-term plasticity —causes→ monosynaptic
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: On finer timescales, putative monosynaptic interactions reflected short-term plasticity in their dynamic and predictable modulation across various aspects of the task, beyond a statistical accounting for the effect of the neurons’ co-varying firing rates.

span.label: facilitation —contrasted-with→ depression
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — both found, and elsewhere BOTH ON ONE POSTSYNAPTIC CELL from different presynaptic partners, which is what rules out passive membrane properties
span.quote: Seeking potential mechanisms for such effects, we found evidence for both firing pattern–dependent facilitation and depression, as well as for a supralinear effect of presynaptic coincidence on the firing of postsynaptic targets.

span.label: RETRACTED (REVERSED) · supralinear —causes→ dendritic spikes
span.note: RETRACTED: REVERSED. The span offers dendritic spikes as the MECHANISM UNDERLYING the supralinear summation, so the spikes produce the supralinearity. — strength of the relation: 0.7 — offered as a candidate mechanism, by analogy to hippocampal neurons
span.quote: One mechanism underlying the supralinear summation effect might be the initiation of dendritic spikes triggered by supersynchronous inputs, as shown in hippocampal neurons 30 . Such dendritic boosting may be particularly prominent in certain interneuron types because of the high densities of voltage-gated sodium and potassium ion channels in distal dendrites

span.label: central arm —operationalised-as→ goal representation
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: differential firing in the shared arm, BEFORE the paths diverge, is what makes it goal rather than movement
span.quote: However, by considering separately the trials in which the rat ran to the left reward area and those in which the rat ran to the right, we see that the neuron already showed a goal-specific elevation of discharge in the central arm itself, suggestive of goal representation.

span.label: cell assemblies —part-of→ mPFC
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — distributed across a large volume with no spatial clustering of similar tuning
span.quote: Neurons active at any given part of the maze were recorded with equal probability at all probe shanks, and we found no evidence for spatial clustering of neurons with similar task-relevant firing patterns. Thus, information in mPFC appears to be sparsely encoded by cell assemblies distributed in a large neuronal volume.

span.label: silicon probe —operationalised-as→ mPFC
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — positioned for superficial or deep layers, which is what makes the layer comparison possible at all
span.quote: The tips of the silicon probes were positioned to record from either the superficial (layers 2/3) or deep (layer 5) layers of the mPFC

span.label: working memory —operationalised-as→ mPFC
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: In this study, we examined large-scale recordings of neuronal activity in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of the rat during a working memory task.

span.label: resampling / surrogate data methods
span.quote: Resampling methods are the primarily statistical tool used to identify (i) conditional differences in firing rates, (ii) monosynaptic interactions and (iii) regions of excess monosynaptic interactions in the maze.

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: Significant differences of peak heights were computed by a permutation test (shuffling the first spike, second~ spike labels, P < 0.10, two-sided test; one side corresponds ‘facilitation’, the other to ‘depression’).

span.label: spike-jitter resampling for cross-correlogram significance
span.quote: Because the jittered data sets preserve firing rates on timescales much broader than that of the jitter interval, the overall effect of the analysis is to identify as monosynaptic those pairs that showed excess co-firing at short latencies that cannot be accounted for by firing rates varying only at timescales of tens of milliseconds

span.label: kernel density estimation
span.quote: We use gaussian kernels of bandwidth σ = 0.05 in normalized length.

span.quote: Thus, one would like to define an error as any false rejection across multiple time indexes and be able to control this (global or family-wise) error rate (FWER) directly

span.label: THE STANDARD ASSUMPTION IS REJECTED BY NAME: under independence, broad-timescale effects alone can raise short-latency co-occurrence above chance
span.quote: Seeking more formal criteria for large scale analysis, a standard approach is to assume that spike trains are independent of one another (that is, precisely, that the response of one neuron is conditionally exchangeable across trials, or shifts, given the other neuron) and then to infer a monosynaptic interaction when the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets is greater than would be expected under independence 15 – 18 , as in the shift predictor. However, such an identification may be confounded by effects occurring more slowly than the timescale of synaptic action: broad-timescale effects alone can cause the co-occurrence of spikes at short-latency offsets to exceed that expected under independence

span.quote: Despite the high-density recordings provided by silicon probes, only a small percentage of neurons and their connections could be monitored in our study (see Supplementary Note ). Because of current limitations in the extracellular method, only neurons with < 60 μm lateral distance from recording sites in the hippocampus generate spikes with sufficiently large amplitudes to be reliably separated into single-neuron clusters 32 . Assuming a similar spike amplitude attenuation in mPFC, the number of recordable neurons from a cylinder of 60-μm radius around each shank corresponds to approximately 60–100 neurons from layer 2/3 and 60 from layer 5 (ref. 22 ), corresponding to a total of 480 to 800 neurons in the volume surveyed by the eight recording shanks. Of these, only approximately 10–25% were active enough in aspects of our task to be clustered. Taking into consideration the ‘silent’ majority, the global firing rate of the population can be estimated as 0.2–0.6 Hz, although individual neurons could robustly increase their spike rates according to task demands. A similar conclusion can be reached by assessing the population synchrony. Of the active minority, on average, approximately 10% of layer 2/3 and 20% of layer 5 neurons fired at least one spike in any 100-ms time window, suggesting that only 1 to 5% of all (active and ‘silent’) neurons fired in synchrony.
